cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Emotional Interest
cards.instruction: Treat comfort, vulnerability, and forgiveness as investments that must eventually be repaid with equal emotional risk.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. I told your mother I'm scared she dislikes me. Sunday, you owe me an equally embarrassing admission.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I didn't ask you to tell her.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. I trusted you to risk something too. What scares you?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's equal. Now tell her over lunch. Mine had an audience; yours needs one too.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 declares a debt, A3 dismisses objections and requires a fear, and A5 approves its value but orders a matching audience.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 disputes the unsolicited investment; A3 insists on reciprocal risk; B4 fear causes A5 equivalence judgment.

relationship.evidence: B2 has a credible objection to a debt never agreed, and B4 nevertheless offers something personal.

heightening.evidence: A5 adds the original audience as the condition for equal repayment after B4 admission.

specificity.evidence: A1 mother and Sunday, A5 lunch, define a concrete emotional repayment venue.
